name: select_tut
description: The select() and pselect() system calls are used to monitor multiple file descriptors for readiness, allowing programs to wait for I/O events or exceptional conditions efficiently. This page provides tutorial information on their use, including handling signals and data events.

parameters.name: nfds
parameters.description: The highest-numbered file descriptor plus one to be monitored

parameters.name: readfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for readability

parameters.name: writefds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for writability

parameters.name: exceptfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for exceptional conditions

parameters.name: sigmask
parameters.description: Signal mask for pselect() to handle signals

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors ready for the requested I/O
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error and sets errno

errors.description: A signal was caught, interrupting the call

bugs: Programs using select() may encounter race conditions if signals arrive after checking global flags but before the call, potentially causing indefinite blocking; pselect() is recommended to mitigate this.
examples: int main(int argc, char *argv[]) { sigset_t sigmask, empty_mask; /* ... code as in the man page ... */ r = pselect(nfds, &readfds, &writefds, &exceptfds, NULL, &empty_mask); }
